Manny Albam is one of America’s most prolific and innovative composers in jazz, classical and film music. He was born in 1922 in the Dominican Republic and grew up in New York City. He worked as a saxophonist with numerous big bands in the 40s and devoted himself to full time writing in 1951. Manny’s scores have been played by a long list of jazz luminaries including Gerry Mulligan, Count Basie, Carmen McRae and Dizzy Gillespie. His original compositions include chamber music and large scale pieces for studio orchestras. Manny has taught at the Eastman School of Music and Glassboro State College and maintains a busy schedule fulfilling commissions and sharing his knowledge with young writers.
Manny was interviewed in Tarrytown, New York on October 31, 1998, by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
